transcript.text: Hi, I've got a Dyson V15 Detect (SV22) about 4 months old. When I go from the kitchen tiles onto the lounge rug the motor suddenly gets much louder and the battery number drops faster, then it calms down again when I go back on the tiles. Also the screen goes up and down by itself. Is the motor on its way out? It's still under guarantee so I want to report it before it dies completely.

It is unlikely that your motor is failing. The Dyson V15 Detect is designed to automatically increase suction when it detects carpet pile, which explains both the louder noise and the faster battery drain on rugs; this is normal operation for 'Auto' mode. However, the screen fluctuating by itself suggests a possible software glitch or sensor issue rather than a mechanical fault. To confirm if this is just the auto-suction working as intended, please switch the vacuum to 'Max' or 'Eco' mode and test it on both surfaces again.

I tried Eco and it stays the same quiet sound on both the rug and the tiles. There's no 'Max' on mine, only Eco, Auto and Boost, and Boost is loud all the time without changing. There's no burning smell, heat or warning lights either. The screen does say 'Auto', so is that what's causing it?

Yes, 'Auto' is exactly what's causing the noise and battery drain. In Auto mode, the V15 uses its laser to count dust particles; when it detects more on your rug, it automatically ramps up suction to clean it deeper, which makes it louder and uses more power. This is normal behaviour for that setting. The screen fluctuating by itself is likely a separate software glitch or sensor quirk rather than a sign of motor failure. Since the vacuum works fine in Eco mode (constant quiet sound) and you have no warning lights or heat, the motor is healthy. I would suggest resetting the unit by turning it off, removing the battery for 30 seconds, then reinserting it to see if the screen stabilises. If the screen continues to jump around erratically after a reset, that specific display/sensor issue can be covered under your guarantee.

candidates: Auto-mode suction adjustment reacting to carpet pile (high)
LCD screen glitch or sensor interference (medium)
